name: Sun Valley
summary: America's original destination ski resort in summer bloom — mountain trails, a charming town, and Hemingway's final home.

lodging.name: A Ketchum or Sun Valley lodge
lodging.blurb: At the base of Bald Mountain.

foodMustTry.name: Idaho trout & a mountain dinner
foodMustTry.blurb: Ketchum punches above its weight for food.

item.title: Bald Mountain
item.blurb: Three thousand four hundred feet of continuous fall-line, and a strong argument for the best ski mountain in America — no flats, no traverses, just top to bottom. In summer the lift runs to the Roundhouse and the trails are yours on foot or on a bike.

item.title: Ketchum & Hemingway's grave
item.blurb: The mountain town where Hemingway lived, died, and is buried, plus his memorial up Trail Creek.

item.title: Sun Valley Lodge & the world's first chairlift

location.name: Sun Valley Lodge
location.address: 1 Sun Valley Rd, Sun Valley, ID

item.blurb: America's first destination ski resort, built in 1936 by the Union Pacific to give people a reason to ride its trains west. Its engineers adapted a machine used to load bananas onto boats and invented the chairlift here — the original is on display. The lodge corridors are lined with photographs of everyone who came: Hemingway finished For Whom the Bell Tolls in room 206.

commute.scenicNote: North over the mountains into Montana.
